statements: cside says several candidates reached technical interviews in a coordinated pattern the founder assessed as North Korean infiltration attempts; none obtained access to cside systems.
Reported outcome: No access and no successful hire reported.
limitations: Do not identify any candidate or current account.
Do not infer nationality or DPRK affiliation from name, accent, appearance, background noise, or scripted answers.
Do not count the several hundred resumes as malicious applicants.
Applicant-stage reporting does not establish a successful hire, system access, post-hire conduct, or harm unless the cited source expressly says so.
No applicant, worker, identity-theft victim, current account, private customer, or anonymized legal entity may be identified or inferred from this record.

Appearance, accent, nationality, ethnicity, language, geography, remote-work preference, camera behavior, VPN use, or any single device, network, phone, or account-age signal is not attribution evidence by itself.

sources.support: Provenance: The author, cside founder Simon Wijckmans, describes cside's own hiring process. The live URL returned a later 404 during this pass; the exact first-party page was recovered from an Internet Archive capture dated 2025-10-14. The post says cside received several hundred resumes for a senior full-stack role, advanced several candidates after assessments, then had three or four near-identical interviews. The author characterizes these as organized North Korean attempts and states explicitly that the actor did not obtain access to any cside system. Normalized boundary: cside says several candidates reached technical interviews in a coordinated pattern the founder assessed as North Korean infiltration attempts; none obtained access to cside systems. Attribution boundary: First-party company assessment, not a government or judicial attribution. Publication boundary: Applicant-stage incident only. Do not create a worker identity, successful-hire record, compromise record, or nationality-based screening rule
